title: Flexible Commit Bundles & Burst Credits — Dedicated Capacity Pricing Experiment
creator: Alicia Park
description:
Background: Enterprise prospects and current Dedicated customers routinely ask for predictable GPU spend with the ability to handle traffic spikes. Our existing reserved model (flat committed GPUs) is simple but inflexible: it either over-commits capacity for peak traffic or requires customers to buy large buffers they seldom use. We need a pricing/packaging experiment that balances predictability for customers and predictable revenue for Redwood, while preserving the operational guarantees Dedicated provides (isolation, SLA, regional continuity).

Goal: Run a controlled experiment to compare three product offers and evaluate unit economics, conversion, churn risk, and sales friction: (A) Fixed commits (baseline) — 3/12 month reserved GPUs at tiered discounts; (B) Flexible Commits — smaller committed baseline + monthly top-up commitment window; (C) Flexible + Burst Credits — small commit + pooled burst credits and autoscaling credits for short spikes.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Flexible Commits with modest discounts will convert more proof-of-concept and mid-market customers than large fixed commits, increasing ARR while reducing upfront friction.
- H2: Adding Burst Credits (prepaid GPU-hour credits usable for 30d bursts) will reduce over-commit purchases while preserving revenue capture on peak usage.
- H3: An explicit autoscaling credit mechanism (credits consumed when autoscale expands beyond commit) will allow us to keep SLOs with predictable revenue and fewer manual quota changes.

Experiment design:
- Cohorts: 1) New inbound trial customers targeted by Sales SDRs; 2) Current customers with predictable seasonality (invite-only); 3) Renewal cohort.
- Offer structure: commit options of 2, 8, or 24 vGPU-equivalent units; commit terms 1m/3m/12m; discount curves modeled in spreadsheet attachment. Burst credits sold in packages (100h, 500h, 2k h) per month; unused credits roll for 30d only. Autoscaling credits consumed per-minute when the runtime provisions > commit baseline.
- SLA tiers: Bronze (99.5% uptime, standard support), Silver (99.9% uptime, 8x5 support, 10% credit on violation), Gold (99.95% uptime, 24x7 support, 25% credit on violation). Pricing delta and eligibility criteria will be documented.
- Contract terms & security questionnaire considerations: standard enterprise MSAs must include data residency region, KMS/HSM integration, audit log retention, SOC2 attestation, penetration test schedule, and explicit language for dedicated pool isolation. Legal to draft addendum for Burst Credits and early termination/true-up.

Success metrics (primary):
- Win rate for deals > $100k ARR across cohorts (target +12% vs baseline over 8 weeks)
- Commits sold as % of total Dedicated revenue (target 20% increase in smaller-commit adoption)
- Effective price per vGPU-hour and projected gross margin >= 45% after infra costs
- Reduction in manual quota change tickets by 30%

Operational considerations and trade-offs:
- Capacity fragmentation: smaller commits + bursts may increase scheduling complexity and reduce packing efficiency. Engineering must model fragmentation delta (ENG-4319).
- Billing complexity: require changes to billing pipeline and usage attribution for autoscaling credit consumption (ENG-4380).
- Sales/Legal complexity: new contract language and quote templates; sales enablement required to avoid over-discounting.
- Observability: Console must show committed baseline, burst credit balance, and autoscale events per token/route for customer transparency.

Deliverables:
- Pricing bands and commitment productized SKUs (separate SKUs for commit term and burst credit packs).
- Legal addendum draft covering burst credits, termination, data residency and audit logs.
- Billing prototype in sandbox and integration test with ERP/billing system.
- Sales one-pager, quote templates, and playbook for SDR/AE.
- Dashboard tiles in Console for customers showing commit vs usage and burst credit burn.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Customers game burst credits and rely on them continuously -> mitigate via hard caps, expirations, and rising price curve after threshold.
- Risk: Operational overhead for on-call due to aggressive autoscale -> define autoscale safe limits and SLO cost threshold.
- Risk: Legal pushback on early termination -> ensure clear pro-rata true-up and minimum notice windows.

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Finalize pricing curves and run unit economics modeling (Alicia + Finance) — due 2025-11-12.
2) Legal to draft addendum and security questionnaire responses for commit offers (Rina) — due 2025-11-18.
3) Eng to scope billing and telemetry changes (ENG-4380 kickoff) — due 2025-11-14.
4) Sales enablement draft and pilot with 5 target accounts (Marcus + Olivia) — kickoff 2025-11-20.

Longer-term: If experiment meets success metrics after 8 weeks, prepare productization plan (pricing catalog, GA rollout, playbooks) and follow-on engineering work to optimize packing kernels for higher fragmentation scenarios.

AC2: Legal addendum for committed capacity reviewed and approved by Legal
AC3: Billing prototype in sandbox records commit baseline vs autoscale usage and burst credit consumption
AC4: Sales one-pager, quote templates, and enablement deck ready for pilot
notes: Trade-off: larger commit discounts reduce ability to upsell and can increase capacity fragmentation
Decision: run experiment for 8 weeks with two cohorts (small commit vs small commit + burst credits); measure conversion and churn risk
Follow-up: econ review and rollback plan after pilot; must include default reversion path for customers who abused burst credits
